projects.name: Lakshya Hub
projects.description: An AI-assisted job-search workspace combining discovery, résumé preparation and application tracking. I’m bringing previously separate résumé tooling into the same product.
projects.problem: A job search is a sequence of connected decisions, but the work often lives in separate places: a résumé, a list of openings and a record of applications. Moving between them makes it harder to keep context and decide what deserves attention next.
projects.approach: I’m connecting search adapters, persistent application data and résumé preparation in one workspace. A shared, canonical résumé state keeps editing and downstream views aligned.
projects.tradeoff: When multiple copies of résumé data produced inconsistent behaviour, I prioritised a canonical-state refactor over another symptom-level patch.
projects.limitations: In active development. The live product and dated build notes may represent different stages.
projects.artifact: The public product is linked below. The diagram on this page is an original illustration of the workflow, not a product screenshot or a measured result.
projects.question: How do you keep a connected workflow working from the same source of truth?

projects.name: PAARTH
projects.line: A working method for AI-assisted coding.
projects.description: PAARTH, formerly SuperAgent, is an open-source layer I built around AI coding tools: workflow routing, persistent memory, action checks and cost controls.
projects.problem: Coding assistants can lose project context between sessions, repeat setup and apply inconsistent workflows across tools.
projects.approach: I built a reusable layer around existing coding assistants, connecting task routing, project memory, action checks and budget visibility through inspectable local files.
projects.tradeoff: Keeping the system as a layer lets it work with existing tools. The integration must respect each tool’s capabilities rather than assume every platform supports the same hooks.
projects.limitations: Public open-source project under active development. The repository documents current capabilities and platform differences.
projects.artifact: Conceptual workflow. Earlier writing uses the former name, SuperAgent.
projects.question: How do you make AI-assisted engineering more consistent across tools?

projects.name: FRIDAY
projects.line: A personal agent, built around local constraints.
projects.description: A local-first personal agent in Python, exploring how orchestration, memory and review can work within the limits of a personal machine.
projects.problem: A personal agent needs to preserve context and use tools without assuming unlimited compute or uninterrupted access to hosted models.
projects.approach: I’m building the orchestration, memory and control layers, with different execution modes for different levels of work.
projects.tradeoff: Local resource limits shape the architecture: tasks should receive an appropriate amount of compute, with checks around tool use.
projects.limitations: In development. Core systems are implemented; further integration and evaluation remain ongoing.
projects.artifact: Conceptual workflow based on my project account.
projects.question: How much machinery does this task actually need?

projects.name: PAARTH-TRADER
projects.description: A local-first trading research system I’m developing to compare strategies and model choices through controlled paper-trading experiments.
projects.problem: A convincing trading demonstration is not evidence that a strategy is ready for real capital. Research needs repeatable comparisons and explicit limits.
projects.approach: I’m building an experimental workflow around candidate comparison, readiness checks and staged evaluation in simulated trading.
projects.tradeoff: Progression depends on evidence from evaluation. The system remains a research project using paper trading, rather than a live-money product.
projects.limitations: Paper-trading research only. No live-money operation or investment-performance claim.
projects.artifact: Conceptual workflow based on my project account.
projects.question: What evidence should be required before an experiment advances?

projects.name: insanemesh.ai
projects.line: From an idea to a reviewable draft.
projects.description: An independent content automation workflow I built to connect drafting, asset creation and human review.
projects.problem: Generating a draft is only one part of publishing. Repeated handoffs make a content workflow difficult to follow and maintain.
projects.approach: I separated idea development, asset creation and review into distinct stages, with a human decision before publication.
projects.tradeoff: Automating preparation saves repeated work. Keeping publication behind review preserves an intentional decision about what leaves the system.
projects.limitations: Documented in a dated public build note. The article describes the workflow at that point in its development.
projects.artifact: Conceptual workflow based on the public build note.
projects.question: Where should automation hand the decision back?
